column1: 2.5.2 The Steady State Consider a steady-state equilibrium of this model in which all real variables (including m) are constant and shocks are set to zero. It follows immediately from (2.56) that 1 þ rss 1⁄4 b1 and from (2.57) that fkðkss; nss; 0Þ 1⁄4 b1 1 þ d: ð2:61Þ Thus, the marginal product of capital is a function only of b and d. If the production function exhibits constant returns to scale, fk will depend only on the capital-labor ratio kss=nss. In this case, (2.61) uniquely determines k=n. That is, the capital-labor ratio is independent of inflation or the real quantity of money.
